summary: The run developed a damage-heavy Ironclad deck and reached Act 2 with adequate tools, but it accumulated substantial damage in the Book of Stabbing fight and died while still leaving defensive actions available. The clearest immediate error was prioritizing offense on the final turn despite having only 14 HP and facing an attack. Earlier card choices also favored adding more attacks, making future draws less consistent and reducing the value of defensive hands.

lessons.title: At critical HP, take the guaranteed defense before attacking
lessons.situation: When HP is low, the enemy is attacking, and a defensive card is legal, especially on a turn where the fight is not already guaranteed to end.
lessons.lesson: Prioritize immediate block and survival over multi-card offense. In the Book of Stabbing fight, do not spend all available energy on attacks when a Defend is still legal; reassess whether preserving one more turn is more valuable than modest extra damage.
evidence_points: Turn 4 began at 14/72 HP with 4 energy, 0 block, and Book of Stabbing intending to attack; Defend was explicitly among the legal alternatives.
Instead, Uppercut, Shockwave, and Whirlwind+ were played, leaving 0 block before the enemy's attack.
lessons.reasoning: This is the strongest directly supported combat mistake: the final state presented a legal defensive action while the player was at lethal-risk HP, yet all energy was committed to offense. The run ended immediately after this sequence, so future decisions should first secure survival unless lethal damage is clearly established.

lessons.title: Stop adding attacks once the deck already has sufficient damage
lessons.situation: After obtaining several damage and scaling cards early, when later rewards offer more attacks alongside skip or utility options.
lessons.lesson: Become more selective with card rewards and skip mediocre attacks to preserve draw consistency. After acquiring Anger, Inflame, Whirlwind+, Sword Boomerang, Rampage, and other attacks, later rewards should be judged mainly by defensive value, draw, scaling, or essential utility rather than simply adding more damage.
evidence_points: The run repeatedly took attack cards including Anger, Whirlwind, Sword Boomerang, Rampage, Headbutt, Pummel, Carnage, Cleave+, and Clothesline+.
The final build contained 25 cards and remained heavily attack-oriented, including Heavy Blade, Whirlwind+, Sword Boomerang, Rampage, Carnage, Pummel, Cleave+, and Clothesline+.
lessons.reasoning: The trajectory shows a persistent pattern of accepting attack-heavy rewards, and the final deck confirms that these additions became permanent rather than temporary combat choices. A smaller, more selective deck would make key defensive cards and scaling pieces appear more reliably.

lessons.title: Treat Coffee Dripper as a commitment to preserving HP
lessons.situation: When selecting Coffee Dripper and entering the next act without a normal healing option at campfires.
lessons.lesson: After taking Coffee Dripper, avoid unnecessary chip damage and value defensive combat lines more highly; HP should be treated as a finite resource because routine campfire healing is no longer available.
evidence_points: The Act 1 boss reward chosen was Coffee Dripper, and it was the only boss relic selected.
After that choice, the Act 2 strategic log shows smithing at floor 23 but no rest action, while the run entered the final Book of Stabbing combat at 63/72 HP and fell to 14/72 during the fight.
lessons.reasoning: Coffee Dripper increases the cost of taking avoidable damage because the logged post-boss route does not show a later rest. The HP decline before and during the final combat supports using more conservative combat decisions once this relic is chosen.
